acceptance.criterion_verbatim: is the per-firm key a STRUCTURAL tenancy boundary (so another firm's starred set is unreachable, not merely unfiltered), and is the marker genuinely inert -- including transitively, where a star writes a row that some other job later treats as a work queue? The transitive path is the one a direct test can miss.
acceptance.output_evidence: STRUCTURAL BOUNDARY: list_starred(firm_id) issues one DynamoDB Query keyed on _partition_key(firm_id) (WATCHLIST#<firm_id>) against the base table's hash key -- Query returns ONLY items whose partition key equals the given value; there is no scan and no code path that receives another firm's rows to filter after the fact (test_starred_watchlist_tenancy_boundary_across_firms asserts both the result and that each firm's own Query call carries only that firm's own key). INERTNESS, DIRECT: star()/unstar() make exactly one call each against the persistence seam; comp-find finds zero hits for harvest/refresh/enqueue/trigger inside lib/research/watchlist/ (AC3). INERTNESS, TRANSITIVE -- THE LIMIT OF WHAT THIS INSTANCE CAN CLAIM: no job anywhere in this repo currently reads the WATCHLIST# partition-key namespace (comp-find over lib/ and infra/ for 'WATCHLIST#' at this commit returns only this cell's own store.py, __init__.py, test and design-record hits -- a fact about the estate's CURRENT state, not a structural guarantee against a FUTURE job being wired to read it as a work queue). The socket-level test guard (block_all_sockets) would catch a DIRECT vendor call added inside star()/unstar(), and the exact-call-count assertions catch a silently-added SECOND row on the same seam (both reproduced firing in controls.mutant below) but neither can see a SEPARATE, later-written job that independently queries WATCHLIST# rows and acts on them -- that risk is named, not closed, by this cell's own design (marker table, no queue, no event source mapping, no stream consumer declared on opal-amgt-security-metrics by this cell or any other cell at this commit).

mutant.description: TWO mutants were tried, in order. (1) star() was temporarily edited to add a REAL socket call (socket.create_connection to example.com:80) after its put_item. Running the full suite showed only 3 of 5 tests failing -- the 2 AC1 tests (test_starred_watchlist_is_shared_across_firm_pms, test_starred_watchlist_tenancy_boundary_across_firms) do not use the block_all_sockets fixture, so the injected call was not intercepted by those two and a REAL outbound TCP connection attempt to example.com (an IANA-reserved documentation/testing domain, no payload sent beyond the handshake) was made from this worktree without being caught -- an unintended, if minor, live network act this instance discloses rather than hides. That mutant was reverted immediately (git diff --stat: no diff) and REPLACED with (2), a network-free mutant: star() edited to make a SECOND table.put_item call (a synthetic 'QUEUE#pending-collection' row) after the real marker write, on the SAME already-faked persistence seam -- zero real network risk, since it never leaves the fake table. This second mutant is the one graded below; both edits were reverted and lib/research/watchlist/store.py is confirmed byte-identical to commit 61770a9396a9a876133b515ae774113ce92fdeb0 (git diff --stat: no output) before this instance's formal AC1-AC3 runs were taken.
